messages:
Sean Gallagher: we need to lock paging policy for the nightly perf baseline jobs before we flip them on for everyone. what’s a page vs noise, and who owns reruns? also: please anchor on the SRE runbook draft in Drive (still WIP) https://drive.google.com/.../perf-baseline-nightly-runbook-draft

Aisha Bello: +1. current alert rules in the draft dashboard PR look like they’ll fire any time p99 moves >5% which is… a lot.

Sergio Costa: yeah, the Grafana alert JSON is currently “warn-only” everywhere but it still spams #eng-sre. we should define: (1) when do we page, (2) when do we just post a summary, (3) when do we auto-rerun.

Allison Grant: also we need to be careful with metric cardinality. if we alert on every (model, region, hw, traffic_shape) tuple, it’s going to be a waterfall. maybe page only on a small “golden set” + aggregate views.

PerfCanaryBot: Nightly baseline run scheduled: 02:00 UTC. Targets: 3 regions x 2 hardware pools x 6 traffic shapes. Artifacts will be uploaded to s3://perf-baselines/q1-2026/nightly/ …

Sean Gallagher: proposal to start (happy to edit):
- Page only on “can’t trust the results” + “severe perf regression on golden set that persists after rerun”.
- Everything else: Slack summary + ticket.
Golden set = top 2 models + top 3 traffic shapes (interactive streaming, interactive non-streaming, bursty concurrency).

Kira Volkov: from regression tooling side: we can classify failures into 3 buckets automatically:
A) runner/infra failure (job failed, missing artifacts, timeouts, upload failed)
B) environment drift (driver/CUDA/runtime build mismatch vs pinned manifest)
C) perf delta (metrics changed vs baseline beyond thresholds)
We should only page for A and B, and for C only if it hits severe thresholds AND survives a rerun.

Marcus Reed: +1 to rerun gate. we had a bunch of “C” in the variance study that were just noisy p99 in eu-west due to fleet mix. i’d rather not wake someone up.

Vanessa Ortiz: re: fleet mix — can we make “B” include GPU SKU composition drift? e.g., if the pool is supposed to be 100% H100 SXM but we get some PCIe nodes, p99 explodes and it’s not a real regression.

Sergio Costa: we can. we’re already stamping `hw_fingerprint` and driver version into the run metadata from the runner. if mismatch vs allowlist -> “environment drift”.

Aisha Bello: can we define explicit thresholds per metric? TTFT vs TPOT vs throughput behave differently. paging on 5% p99 TTFT is too sensitive.

Sean Gallagher: yep. let’s write this down as policy:

1) Alert tiers
- INFO (no human action): post run summary to #eng-runtime-perf + store artifacts
- WARN (triage during business hours): Slack alert + auto-create Linear issue (assigned to perf-suite maintainer)
- PAGE (oncall): PagerDuty page to SRE oncall

2) PAGE conditions
PAGE only if one of:
- Job failed 2x in a row (infra/runner) OR no artifacts posted by 04:30 UTC
- Environment drift detected (driver/CUDA mismatch, runtime build mismatch, hw_fingerprint mismatch) and affects >25% of golden runs
- Severe regression: on golden set, after 1 automatic rerun, regression persists AND exceeds threshold

3) Severe regression thresholds (golden set)
- TTFT p95: +20% or +40ms (whichever larger)
- TTFT p99: +30% or +80ms
- TPOT p95: +15%
- Throughput (tok/s) p50: -15%
- Error rate: +1.0% absolute OR any non-zero 5xx spike >0.5% for >10 min during run
Non-golden shapes only ever WARN (no page).

Does that match expectations?

Allison Grant: looks sane. only tweak: for TTFT absolute thresholds should be shape-dependent (streaming chat tends to have lower baseline TTFT than long-context). but using “whichever larger” helps.

Kira Volkov: +1. also, error rate condition should include “systematic client timeout” (the harness will show it as canceled/timeout not 5xx). we should treat sustained timeout increases as regression.

Marcus Reed: for severe regression: can we require “2 of 3 metrics” rather than a single metric spike? i.e., if only p99 TTFT moved but TPOT + throughput stable, it might be a histogram artifact.

Aisha Bello: careful: for user pain, TTFT alone can be enough. but i like requiring *either* (TTFT severe) OR (TPOT/throughput severe). maybe don’t require 2-of-3, but do require it to persist after rerun + no drift.

Sean Gallagher: ok. we’ll keep TTFT as single-metric page-worthy if it’s severe and persistent.

Sergio Costa: ownership for reruns:
- Auto rerun: perf-canary will rerun once on any “C” classification.
- Manual rerun: SRE oncall triggers rerun if paging condition met and classification is unclear.
Need “who is secondary” from Runtime.

Sean Gallagher: i want primary = SRE oncall only for PAGE events. everything else should go to Runtime perf suite owner.
So:
- WARN issues assign to Marcus Reed (perf suite maintainer) with watchers: Kira + Sergio.
- PAGE wakes SRE; SRE’s job is only to (a) validate environment, (b) rerun once if needed, (c) if persistent, escalate to Runtime perf oncall (or named contact).
Do we have a Runtime contact rotation yet?

Marcus Reed: not formal, but for Q1 we can use #eng-runtime-perf and tag @Noah Patel + @Sofia Ivanova depending on scheduler vs kernel. for overnight pages, having a named fallback is helpful.

Sahana Iyer: release eng POV: we *really* don’t want nightly pages for noise. but we do want a signal if the runner is broken or drift happens, since those invalidate release qualification. paging on A/B makes sense.

Vanessa Ortiz: i can be the “fleet drift” contact for now. if drift triggers a page, SRE can tag me and we can chase the pool config / driver rollout.

PagerDuty: Sean Gallagher updated service “Perf Baseline Nightly” escalation policy. (pending)

Allison Grant: can we document “what SRE should do when paged” as a short checklist in the runbook? e.g. first steps: check run metadata, compare hw_fingerprint, confirm pinned manifest, then rerun.

Sean Gallagher: yep. action items:
- Sean: update runbook draft w/ policy + checklist + escalation contacts (Vanessa for drift, Marcus for suite, Runtime escalation via #eng-runtime-perf + Noah/Sofia)
- Sergio: adjust Grafana alerts: only golden set -> PAGE-capable; all tuples -> WARN/INFO + slack summary
- Kira: implement classification A/B/C in perf-canary summary message + auto-rerun gating
- Aisha: propose SLO-aligned thresholds mapping (esp TTFT) so we’re not alerting on meaningless bumps

Aisha Bello: works. also please add “quiet hours” semantics: WARN alerts should batch into a single morning digest vs pinging at 3am.

Sergio Costa: can do. i’ll make perf-canary post 1 nightly summary thread, and only page on the conditions we listed.

Sean Gallagher: cool. locking this unless objections in next 24h.
:thumbsup:

PerfCanaryBot: Acknowledged. Next run will use alert policy v0.3 (golden set only).
